title: QuickFold hierarchy + edge-case grooming
content:
Context:
This is a working doc from the Console + Rollouts grooming session on 2025-02-11. Purpose: capture a concrete information architecture variant (QuickFold) that aims to reduce lateral navigation between products (models, endpoints, rollouts, billing) while keeping per-route performance and observability surfaces discoverable for platform and SRE users.

High-level goals:
- Reduce time-to-target when users need to perform common tasks (create endpoint, inspect model perf, set canary).
- Keep the left rail slim for new users but expandable for power users.
- Ensure every primary action has a canonical route (URL pattern) and analytics event.
- Preserve Dedicated/Private product separation without deep duplication.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Not addressing global header (org selector) in this doc — separate thread.
- Minimal backend routing work initially: prefer client-side route composition and feature flags for rollout.
- Avoid breaking existing deep-links for major customers (plan: redirect map).

Design summary (QuickFold):
- Single left rail with three hierarchical fold groups: "Workspaces" (org/project switch), "Live" (hosts runtime resources: endpoints, deployments, scaling), and "Manage" (models, rollouts, billing, settings).
- Each group supports an "auto-unfold" rule: if a user last visited an item inside a group within 14 days, that group opens on load.
- Secondary navigation surfaces (contextual tabs) appear within the page header (persistent across subroutes).
- Inline mini-Panels: short previews for common items (e.g., endpoint recent errors, model last-eval) show on hover on desktop, accessible by a keyboard shortcut (Cmd+K then type "peek").

Proposed route patterns (canonical):
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/live/endpoints/:endpointId (endpoint detail)
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/live/endpoints/:endpointId/trace/:traceId (trace view)
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/manage/models/:modelId (model detail)
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/manage/rollouts/:rolloutId (rollout detail)
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/manage/billing (billing overview)
- /orgs/:orgId/projects/:projectId/workspace (project home)

Sidebar states and behavior:
- Collapsed (icons only): keyboard labels remain accessible; tooltips appear after 300ms hover.
- Expanded (labels + icons): default for new users during first 7 days after signup; then shrink by default unless pinned.
- Pinned: users can pin the rail to persist expanded state across devices via user preference. Preference stored server-side (user profile).
- Quick actions: a small floating popout at bottom-left for "+ Create" with most-used primitives (endpoint, model upload, canary).

Edge cases & rules we discussed:
1) Deep link to model eval that belongs to a model in a different project: show a top-banner with context + "Switch to project" button; default is to display in a read-only overlay to preserve mental model.
2) Two-level duplication: models appear under Manage and also under Live->Deployments when deployed. Decision: keep a single source of truth (model detail under Manage). Live pages will show an embedded model-card that links to Manage. Avoid editing model metadata from Live pages (only quick metadata like tag).
3) Large orgs with 100+ projects: left rail resource lists must paginate or allow typeahead. Proposed: replace static project list with search-first UX; show 5 recent projects then "Search projects" text box.
4) Guest user with limited perms: hide actions that are not permitted, but still surface read-only links with a tooltip "Request access" that opens a modal to trigger an invite flow.

Wireframe notes (desktop-first):
- View: Endpoint detail: left rail, main content split with header (name + status + rollout badge), tabbed header [Overview | Traces | Metrics | Revisions], right rail collapsed by default containing quick toggles (scale, edit traffic).
- Mobile: convert left rail to bottom sheet with most-used actions. Secondary tabs become a sticky subheader.
- Hover panels: lightweight (max 280px) with 2 lines summary + 2 CTA buttons (Open, Copy Link). Accessible via keyboard 'Peek' shortcut.

Accessibility considerations:
- All collapse/expand controls must have aria-expanded and be reachable by keyboard alone.
- Tooltips should have accessible alternatives: press-and-hold on touch to show content, and keyboard shortcut to focus peek without hover.
- Color contrast for read/unread badges and status chips must meet AA. Provide textual status alongside chips for colorblind users.

Analytics and events (must emit for each canonical route):
- page.view (route, projectId, orgId, userId)
- nav.sidebar_toggle (state: collapsed|expanded|pinned)
- quick_action.invoke (action: create_endpoint|create_model|start_rollout)
- page.peek (targetType, targetId, method: hover|keyboard)
- deep_link.resolve (originalUrl, finalRoute, redirectReason)
Metrics to track during rollout: time-to-first-action for new users, average clicks-to-endpoint-inspect, percent of sessions using pinned rail, errors on model->endpoint transition.

Backlog grooming notes (prioritized):
1) CORE-1: Implement left rail component with groups + auto-unfold rule (3 wks) — MVP: client-side only, store pin in localStorage. (estimate: 5 dev days + 2 QA)
2) CORE-2: Route canonicalization and redirect map for existing deep-links (2 wks) — must include migration plan for customers with bookmarks. (estimate: 4 dev days)
3) UX-1: Hover peek panel + keyboard shortcut (1 wk) (estimate: 3 dev days)
4) SRE-1: Ensure route-level observability hooks for traces/metrics endpoints (blocking for rollout) (2 wks) (dependence: service team)
5) ACCESS-1: Accessibility QA and fixes (1 wk) (estimate: 5 QA days)
6) MIGRATE-1: Migrate user pin preference server-side and expose via profile API (3 wks) (backend + migration window)

Dependencies & owners:
- Frontend: Marco Liu (owner CORE-1, UX-1)
- Backend / Routing: Benji Morales (owner CORE-2, MIGRATE-1)
- SRE: Priya Desai (owner SRE-1)
- Design: Tess Nguyen (wireframes + accessibility), Aisha (owner of doc + rollout plan)

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha: internal opt-in for 10% of employees — collect qualitative feedback, catch major regressions.
- Beta: feature-flagged across orgs with telemetry; expose pin preference in profile; collect metrics over 2 weeks.
- Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 48h observation windows and automated rollback on key SLO regressions (page-load time, error-rate).

Open questions (follow-ups):
- Should hover peek content be server-rendered to reduce client bundle size? (Benji to investigate caching + partial endpoints.)
- Does auto-unfold time window stay at 14 days or become adaptive (based on recency frequency)? (Design to propose alternate heuristics.)
- Mirror behavior for private deployments (on-prem): can we avoid server-side pin preference? (Ops/legal constraint).

Decisions made today (consensus):
- Keep models canonical under Manage, show embedded model-cards in Live pages.
- Use client-side feature flag for initial rollout to avoid backend migrations up-front.
- Provide a redirect map for existing deep links and surface a banner explaining the change for 30 days after rollout.

Notes to implementers / dev checklist:
- Add unit tests for collapse state transitions and aria attributes.
- Provide instrumentation points for page.peek and nav.sidebar_toggle events.
- Add a migration PR template for deep-link redirects that requires owner approval and a rollback test.

Meeting capture (short):
- 2025-02-11 grooming (45m). Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Tess, Benji, Priya. Outcome: prioritize CORE-1 + CORE-2; Tess to produce high-fidelity endpoint and model detail wireframes by 2025-02-18.

Next steps (this doc):
- Design: deliver HLD & Figma frames for peek panel and endpoint tabs (due 2025-02-18).
- Eng: spike on server-side pin vs localStorage persistence (due 2025-02-20).
- Product: prepare customer comms draft for redirect plan (due 2025-02-25).

Notes to self: keep this doc as an evolving single source-of-truth for QuickFold. Move to "final" when backend migrations are committed and redirect map validated.
